title: Surface same-partition Richards fail-closed numerical-domain characterization
central_question: Why do the P4 SURF_P same-partition Richards routes leave the frozen qualified numerical domain, and is the fail-closed boundary caused by the existing fixed integrated local-residual allowance rather than loss of solver state integrity or head convergence?

hypotheses.H1: Failing routes terminate in strict_first_sample under RETRY_LOCAL_BALANCE with head_flags=0 and finite total residual already within the prospective representation bound.
hypotheses.H2: The terminal failure is specifically the pre-existing local_integrated <= 1.6e-15 cm fail-closed check, not a changed solver convergence criterion.
hypotheses.H3: Failure incidence depends on material, vertical partition and temporal factor because the fixed absolute integrated-local-residual allowance interacts with the resolved residual magnitude and transaction duration.
hypotheses.H4: Successful routes remain bitwise O0/O2 identical under the unchanged numerical policy; failing routes show the same diagnostic failure signature across O0/O2.

observables: last accepted CASE and STEP before failure

decision_logic.CONTRACT_BOUNDARY_SUPPORTED: All observed fail-closed routes terminate at the unchanged local integrated-residual allowance with RETRY_LOCAL_BALANCE, zero head flags, and O0/O2-identical diagnostic signature; successful routes never cross the allowance.
decision_logic.MIXED_NUMERICAL_FAILURE: At least one failing route has a different failure class, nonzero head flags, nonfinite diagnostic quantity, or O0/O2 disagreement.
decision_logic.DIAGNOSTIC_INCOMPLETE: Instrumentation cannot identify the terminal fail-closed condition for one or more failing routes.

prohibited: relax or scale the 1.6e-15 cm allowance
change solver physics or constitutive functions
continue a route after the original fail-closed require
use P5A to claim Layer-ROM closure deficiency
use P5A to admit an application or production ROM
